alignments.note: Waw takes *And*.
Suffix of the possessive `לְ` takes the English subject pronoun of the recast clause (rules 18, 43).
`הָיָה` is present, so it takes the *had* of the recast possessive clause (rule 43).
With `הָיָה` carrying the *had*, the possessive preposition has no English word left (rules 40, 43).
The construct relation is rendered attributively rather than with *of*, so `עֹז` takes *strong* (rule 28).
Construct noun rendered *rods*.
`אֶל` rendered *for*.
Construct noun with no article morpheme present takes the supplied *the* (rule 29).

Anarthrous substantival participle: the ASV supplies *them that* to make it a noun phrase, and no article morpheme is present to take it, so it joins the participle's unit (rule 46). The relational *of* is the construct relation's (rule 19). *bare rule* is a light verb plus complement, so the head is *rule* (rule 44).
Waw takes *and*.
Suffix takes the possessive determiner the ASV writes, *their* (rule 18).
Construct noun keeps its own word.
Finite verb recast with copula and participle; head on the lexical word (rule 24).

`עַל־בֵּין` rendered by the single English word *among*, so the two prepositions share one unit under rule 30, headed on `בֵּין`, which is what *among* says. The competing reading marks `עַל` `unrepresented` and gives *among* to `בֵּין` alone; the one-English-word condition of rule 30 is met here, so I took the fusion.

Anarthrous plural with a supplied definite article (rule 15). Head on *boughs*, the word naming what the lexeme names, with *thick* the specifier (rule 31); the margin's *Or, clouds* does not change the alignment.
Waw takes *and*.
Niphal with supplied subject pronoun and auxiliary; head on the lexical participle.
Preposition rendered *in*.
Suffix takes the possessive *their* (rule 18).
Construct noun keeps its own word.
Preposition rendered *with*.
Construct noun with no article morpheme present takes the supplied *the* (rule 29).
Nomen rectum takes the relational *of* (rule 19); discontinuous around the possessive (rule 25).
Suffix takes the possessive *their* (rule 18).

review_notes: All 25 source and 35 target IDs partitioned exactly once.
The ASV's marginal *Hebrew his* / *Hebrew he was* notes flag number and gender differences between the suffixes and the English pronouns; what the ASV wrote is what is aligned (rule 18).
